sources.entry: Marxico - Delicate Markdown editor for Evernote. Reliable storage and sync.

summary.name: Marxico
summary.one_liner: Marxico is a Markdown editor that stores and syncs its notes through Evernote.
use_cases: writing markdown notes stored in Evernote
editing technical docs with code blocks and LaTeX
drawing flow charts and sequence diagrams in notes
organizing Evernote notes by notebook and tags
summary.what_it_does: Marxico is a Markdown editor whose notes are saved entirely in Evernote, which handles storage and sync. It supports code highlighting, LaTeX expressions, flow charts and sequence diagrams, and inserting images and attachments. It offers live preview, offline docs, a desktop client and an offline Chrome App. A special @(Notebook)[tags] syntax selects the Evernote notebook and tags, and the first heading becomes the note title. Markdown source is kept in a hidden area of saved Evernote notes so it can be edited again.
notable: Stores Markdown source inside Evernote notes so they can be re-edited, with no intermediate server storing content
Supports flow charts, sequence diagrams, LaTeX and code highlighting
Uses @(Notebook)[tag1|tag2] syntax to set Evernote notebook and tags
Listed in awesome-mac under Markdown Tools
caveats: Free trial of 10 days; after that a Pro purchase is needed to sync new notes (previously saved notes stay editable)
Checkboxes cannot be toggled in Evernote; they must be edited in Marxico
Footnotes and TOC do not work because Evernote disables ID attributes
